b-follower-append.rationale: The shutdown residual is replaced by the observation: a clean-copy exploration on a running node saw the heartbeat answered immediately, and the identical call after Raft.Shutdown returned without answering inside a 500 ms window, so the branch drops the request rather than responding. b-follower-append.preserves: b-follower-append keeps its owner, trigger, guards, edges and serialization protections; the three confirmed findings and the bounded restart result are unaffected, and the remaining unknown on that behavior is unchanged.

surface:Raft.processHeartbeat.rationale: The surface reason now states the observed consequence of the shutdown branch alongside the fast-path description, so a reader sees that the unanswered-request question is settled by execution while the serialization question is not.

feedback.answered: The transport heartbeat handler drops a request instead of answering it once the node is shut down: with an identical AppendEntries heartbeat the handler answered immediately while the node ran (responded true, nil error, same-millisecond), and after a clean Raft.Shutdown the same call returned without answering inside a 500 ms observation window (responded false, node state Shutdown). The earlier build failure of this exploration was a harness defect (the RPC response channel is send-only on the target struct) and was repaired before the recorded run.
remaining: The (setState, setCurrentTerm) pair in appendEntries is not atomic as a pair, so an off-thread heartbeat and a concurrent campaign can still interleave at the field level; whether an external reader can observe a term regression is not established (b-follower-append).
Whether the election restriction always keeps truncation above every committed configuration index (b-fsm-apply).
Whether an application FSM that applied entries under an in-memory configuration is consistent with the configuration re-derived after a restart (b-config-change).
The liveness-shaped residuals on pre-vote tally inflation and unvalidated TimeoutNow, and the recovered-index fencing question (b-prevote, b-leadership-transfer, b-offline-recovery).
The two out-of-snapshot questions: callers outside this repository that depend on the configuration index readout, and the general intersecting-majority argument (b-config-readout, f-commit-quorum).

Whether the unanswered heartbeat during shutdown produces an observable cost on a real transport (for example a connection goroutine waiting on the response) is not established; only the in-process handler behaviour was observed.
feedback.rationale: The exploration answered the specific question that the surface and the behavior carried, so the map now states the observed relationship instead of the premise, and the wider transport-level cost is named as the independent question that remains. Unit admission is exhausted, so no obligation was created and the execution adds construction knowledge, not property Evidence.
